conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the claim is true and provides multiple authoritative sources demonstrating that Kyleena is FDA-approved for pregnancy prevention for up to five years.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
The claim is **true**, not false. Multiple authoritative sources confirm that Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system) is FDA-approved for pregnancy prevention for up to five years.

**Key evidence:**

- The FDA approved Kyleena on September 16, 2016, specifically for “prevention of pregnancy for up to five years,” as stated in Bayer’s press release announcing the approval ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fda-approves-bayers-kyleena-levonorgestrel-releasing-intrauterine-system-195-mg-for-prevention-of-pregnancy-for-up-to-five-years-300330006.html)).
- Healion reported that “the FDA has approved Kyleena for the prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years” ([Healio](https://www.healio.com/news/primary-care/20160920/fda-approves-bayer-iud-kyleena)).
- The official Kyleena prescribing information states: “Kyleena® (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system) is a hormone-releasing IUD that prevents pregnancy for up to 5 years” ([Kyleena patient site](https://www.kyleena-us.com/prescribing-information)).
- Drugs.com similarly notes the device is placed “to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years” ([Drugs.com](https://www.drugs.com/kyleena.html)).

Clinical data support this duration: a Phase 3 study with an optional extension to five years demonstrated a cumulative failure rate of approximately 1.4% over that period, with more than 99% efficacy per year of use.

**Conclusion:** The view that the claim is false is incorrect. The evidence consistently shows Kyleena is FDA-approved for pregnancy prevention for up to five years.
